source_edits.old: RankCloak provides a way to carry cryptographic artifacts in generated text without displaying their recognizable syntax, together with a framework for measuring how reliably they can be recovered. We first test recovery with the original token sequence preserved, then examine what happens when the receiver converts visible text back into tokens or receives an edited version. We also assess how easily encoded messages can be detected, how entropy-based selection of embedding positions and model precision affect performance, and whether complete messages remain understandable. Two local model judges assess each message in context, allowing minor awkwardness when its meaning remains understandable. Their scores measure automated acceptability; human perception was not assessed. Exact replay depends on shared model and protocol settings, which enable compatible decoding but do not themselves provide cryptographic secrecy.

source_edits.old: RankCloak keeps the cover side rank transfer idea from Calgacus, but changes the payload-side representation. Instead of relying only on direct LLM tokenization of the displayed artifact, RankCloak maps serialized artifact strings into explicit bounded rank sequences.
